title: the last morning
narrativeQuestion: Everyone knew the war would end at 11:00. What did commanders do with the six hours?

chapters.title: The signatures
chapters.claim: The armistice was signed about 5:12 and set the end at 11:00.

chapters.title: The car
chapters.claim: Dining car 2419D was Foch's office and later Hitler's stage.

chapters.title: What Germany agreed to
chapters.claim: The terms stripped Germany of the means to fight and move an army.

chapters.title: Why wait until 11
chapters.claim: The hour had to travel and had a ring to it, and attacks were not ordered to stop.

chapters.title: The six hours
chapters.claim: Most of the last day's losses came after the signing.

chapters.title: The last four
chapters.claim: Four armies each remember a last man killed.

chapters.title: Henry Gunther
chapters.claim: Gunther was killed at 10:59 charging a machine gun.

chapters.title: Why attack at all
chapters.claim: The reasons given and what the record says about them.

chapters.title: From Armistice Day to Veterans Day
chapters.claim: The day became a holiday and was renamed in 1954.
